docs.title: ip_info
docs.text:
A Python command-line tool for quickly querying IP address information from multiple providers.

In security work you often need geolocation and reputation information for an IP address, and because results are inconsistent between providers the most reliable approach is to check several at once.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Checks up to 15 free providers in parallel and returns results in seconds.
  • Accepts IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and supports bulk queries where the provider allows it.
  • Validates addresses first, discarding invalid and reserved IPs to avoid wasting queries.
  • Keeps a local SQLite database of past queries (90 days by default) to avoid looking up the same IP twice.
  • Can parse IP addresses out of clipboard text for easier multi-IP input.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Install — get ip_info set up with uv or pip.
  • Usage — look up addresses, parse the clipboard, choose the output format and providers.
  • Providers — the supported providers and how to store their API keys.
  • Reference — package API documentation.

docs.title: Recommended: install with uv
docs.text:
If you don't already have it, install uv.

uv tool install git+https://github.com/DrollRobot/ip_info.git

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Installing provides these commands:

Command Purpose ip_info Look up one or more IP addresses (alias: ipi). ip_info_keys Store or update provider API keys.

See Usage to get started.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: ip_info can query the 14 providers below. Four require no registration; the rest offer a free tier that needs an API key. Use the name column with --apis to query a specific provider (see Usage).

docs.title: Adding API keys
docs.text:

To add or update a key, run:

docs.title: Available providers
docs.text: Provider --apis name Key Notes AbstractAPI.com abstractapicom Required High rate limit (1/sec). AbuseIPDB.com abuseipdbcom Required Abuse reports; high limit (1k/day); no location data. CriminalIP.io criminalipio Required Good security information; low limit (50/month). IP-API.com ipdashapicom Not required High rate limit; supports bulk queries. IP2Location.io ip2locationio Optional High limit (1k/day, more with a key); location, ASN, proxy only. IPAPI.co ipapico Not required High limit (1k/day); bulk; location and ASN only. IPAPI.com ipapicom Required Low limit (100/month); location only. IPAPI.is ipapiis Required Security and risk data; high limit (1k/day); bulk. IPAPI.org ipapiorg Required High limit (1k/day); bulk. IPGeolocation.io ipgeolocationio Required High limit (1k/day); location only. IPInfo.io ipinfoio Required No rate limit; location only. IPQuery.io ipqueryio Not required High limit; bulk; good security information. IPRegistry.co ipregistryco Required Good security information; 100k queries per account. VirusTotal.com virustotalcom Required Good security information; trusted provider; low limit (4/min, 500/day).

docs.title: Suggesting a provider
docs.text: Know of a provider that offers API access in a free tier that isn't listed? Contributions are welcome — see CONTRIBUTING.md. Providers that need no key, have a high rate limit, and return good security information (Tor/VPN detection, risk scores, abuse reports) are especially useful.

docs.title: Looking up IP addresses
docs.text:
Pass one or more addresses on the command line:

ip_info 1.2.3.4 8.8.8.8
ipi 1.2.3.4 8.8.8.8         # short alias: ipi
ip_info                     # with no arguments, scans clipboard for ip addresses

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
View the results as a table with --output table (the default):

Or view the raw JSON with --output rawjson:

ip_info 1.2.3.4 --output rawjson

docs.title: Choosing which providers to query
docs.text:
By default, ip_info queries every provider that has a key saved in the keyring, plus every provider that does not require a key.

To query specific providers, use --apis with one or more provider names:

ip_info 1.2.3.4 --apis virustotalcom ipqueryio

Note

The output shows data from every provider that has results saved in the local database for the given IP, even if you only queried a subset this run.

See Providers for the full list of provider names and how to add API keys.
